html:
Tagé Cho Hudän are the Northern Tutchone people of the Little Salmon/Carmacks First Nation, on the Yukon River around the village of Carmacks in central Yukon. They speak an Athabaskan language.

They lived by fishing salmon on the Yukon River, hunting moose and caribou and trading with coastal peoples. Carmacks is named after George Carmack, who with Skookum Jim and Dawson Charlie found the gold on Bonanza Creek that set off the Klondike Gold Rush in 1896. Steamboats and later the highway brought outsiders through their land. The nation signed a self-government agreement in 1997. Neighbours include Selkirk, Na-cho Nyak Dun and Champagne and Aishihik.
